You are auditing a Lean 4 formalization in the project at /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild (project dir; Lean sources under AlgebraicJacobian/).

CONTEXT. The "DD-R certificate" lane needs, for a relative curve `relCurve C R` over a test ring R, a `DivisorAdaptation C R pi d` satisfying `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified n` (defined in AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamily.lean around line 426). A `DivisorAdaptation` is built on `FinCoverData` (DivisorFamily.lean:160): finitely many basic opens `D(h₀ j)` of the pinned chart V₀ and `D(h₁ j)` of the pinned chart V₁, WITH A PARTITION OF UNITY on each chart (`∑ a₀ j * h₀ j = 1`), so the chart-0 pieces cover V₀ and chart-1 pieces cover V₁ (`FinCoverData.cover₀/cover₁`, DivisorFamily.lean:199-207).

I have just proved (in AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean, all kernel-clean) that IF the off-diagonal overlap colength modules `ovlColength i j` (i≠j) all vanish ("support-separated"), THEN the whole certificate reduces to just the (c1) data (each `colength j` finite + projective over R) plus a constant-rank reading — the two hard flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) and the kernel-spanning hypothesis all become free, because the Cech difference `deltaLeft - deltaRight` is literally ZERO. I also proved that an overlap disjoint from `d.supportLocus` has vanishing overlap colength, so it suffices that AT MOST ONE PIECE MEETS THE SUPPORT.

THE QUESTION I need answered rigorously: is that hypothesis actually ACHIEVABLE, or is it self-contradictory? Specifically:

(a) The pieces must COVER each pinned chart (partition of unity). The support (`d.supportLocus`) is the divisor, a degree-g effective divisor, finite over the base. The two pinned charts V₀,V₁ cover the whole relative curve. If the support meets both V₀ and V₁, then chart-0 pieces must cover the part of the support in V₀ and chart-1 pieces the part in V₁ — so at least one piece from EACH chart meets the support, giving TWO support-meeting pieces, and their overlap might meet the support. Investigate: (i) can V₀'s pieces be arranged so exactly one meets the support, and likewise V₁, and can the OVERLAP of those two still avoid the support? (ii) Is there a spelling where the support lies entirely inside ONE chart (e.g. away from the fibre at infinity / the fibre over a point of P1), so all chart-1 pieces avoid it? Look for existing lemmas about where the seed/theta divisor support sits relative to the pinned charts (`relCover`, `fiberTwoCover`, `P1`, `pinnedChart`, `relPinnedChart`).

(b) CRUCIAL SANITY CHECK: is my reduction too good to be true? If a separated adaptation always existed, the certificate — including CONSTANT FIBRE RANK n over a possibly NONREDUCED base R — would follow with no flatness input, which would contradict the recorded fact (memory I-0209 and AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean) that the flatness is genuinely needed. Where exactly does the difficulty move to? My claim is it moves into the (c1) clause `Module.Projective R (colength j)` for the one support-meeting piece j, and into the rank clause. Verify by reading `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean`, `SupportTube.lean` (esp. `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` ~line 329 and `flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` ~line 313) and `SlicingFlat.lean` (`Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField`). Note that lemma needs `[Module.Flat R B]` where B = Γ(relCurve C R, pieces j) — is THAT flatness available/hard? State precisely what the remaining obligations are for a separated adaptation.

(c) Report whether `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_sep` style hypotheses appear anywhere as an already-discharged fact over a RING (not a field). Over a field there is `DivisorFamilyFieldDegree.lean:122 gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated` and `deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated` (DivisorFamilyFieldDegree.lean:398) — check how the FIELD case obtains separation, since that is the template: does something construct a separated adaptation over a field? If yes, does the construction generalize to a ring, and what breaks?

Use the workspace search tool for lemma lookup: `/home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon search "<words>" --json` (indexes this project AND mathlib AND sibling projects). Do NOT grep for lemma names you are guessing. Read files with your Read tool. Do not edit any file. Do not run lake build.

Report: (1) verdict on achievability of the one-support-piece hypothesis, with file:line evidence; (2) the precise list of remaining obligations under my reduction; (3) where the known-hard content actually lives now; (4) whether the field-case separation construction generalizes. Be concrete and skeptical — I would rather learn now that the route is circular than after building on it.

11	/-!
12	# Certified divisor families: the DD-1 carrier (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1)
13	
14	The Wave-4 DAT-D divisor functor's object data over an affine test `R`, the worksheet's
15	(D1) pin (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §1.1): a `LocalEquations` system `d` on the
16	relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R`, a **finite chart adaptation** refining it — finitely
17	many basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts with partition witnesses, carrying
18	regular equations `f_j` that agree with `d`'s equations up to units — and the **colength
19	certificate**: the chart-local colength modules `Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)` are finite projective
20	over `R`, and the glued equalizer module `W(d)` is finite projective of constant fibre
21	rank `n` (`Module.rankAtStalk`), with the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
22	certificates base-change (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`).
23	
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData` — the `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data (`Type u`;
25	  DAT-1's `BasicOpenCoverData` shape is `Type (u+1)`, unusable inside a functor value).
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation` — the adaptation: equations + the pointwise
27	  refinement-up-to-units clause `eqn_rel` (point-free, so it pulls back along arbitrary
28	  morphisms), with the anchored constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`.
29	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule` — the glued colength module
30	  `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺) ⊆ Π_j Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)`, with the equalizer description
31	  `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` (the worksheet's `eq(∏_j ⇉ ∏_{j,j'})`).
32	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` — the certificate (c1)–(c4).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq` — divisor equality of local-equation
34	  systems: on a common refinement the equations agree up to units (refinement +
35	  rescaling in one move), an equivalence relation with
36	  `picClass_eq_of_divEq` (the class laws `picClass_restrict`/`picClass_rescale`).
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily`, `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFam` — the certified
38	  family and the setoid quotient `DivFam C π n R : Type u`, the divisor functor's value
39	  on the affine test `R`, with `DivFam.picClass`.
40	
41	The `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through
42	`relCurve.instOver` (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate the same
43	instances.
44	-/

56	/-! ## Divisor equality of local-equation systems (the setoid relation)
57	
58	Generic in the scheme; this is pure `DivisorClass`-level material. -/
59	
60	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
61	
62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
63	
64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
69	
70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
79	
80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
82	
83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
89	
90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
122	        rw [E2]
123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
125	        rw [mul_assoc]
126	
127	/-- Structure extensionality for local-equation systems: the two `Prop` fields are
128	proof-irrelevant, so a system is determined by its cover and equations. -/
129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)
130	    (heqn : d.eqn ≍ e.eqn) : d = e := by
131	  cases d; cases e
132	  cases hcov; cases heqn
133	  rfl
134	
135	/-- **Divisor equality preserves the Picard class** (`𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor):
136	restrict both systems to the common refinement (`picClass_restrict`), where they differ
137	by a unit rescaling (`picClass_rescale`). -/
138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
139	    d₁.picClass = d₂.picClass := by
140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
141	  rw [← d₁.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₁, ← d₂.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₂]
142	  have hres : d₁.restrict 𝒲 h₁ = (d₂.restrict 𝒲 h₂).rescale (fun x => (H x).choose) := by
143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
144	    exact (H x).choose_spec
145	  rw [hres, picClass_rescale]
146	
147	end Scheme.LocalEquations
148	
149	/-! ## The finite chart adaptation -/
150	
151	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
152	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
153	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
154	
155	/-- **The `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data** of the two pinned charts of the relative
156	curve (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): `m₀ + m₁` basic-open generators with partition
157	witnesses. The DAT-1 datum `BasicOpenCoverData` carries `Type u` index fields and hence
158	lives in `Type (u+1)`; this `Fin`-indexed form is the `Type u` carrier a functor value
159	can quotient. -/
160	structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
161	  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
162	  m₀ : ℕ
163	  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
164	  m₁ : ℕ
165	  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
166	  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
167	  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
168	  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
169	  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
170	  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
171	  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
172	  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
173	  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
174	  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
175	  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
176	  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1
177	
178	namespace FinCoverData
179	
180	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
181	
182	/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
183	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m₀ ⊕ Fin D.m₁
184	
185	/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
186	noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
187	  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
188	    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))

210	/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
211	(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
212	noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
213	    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
214	  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
215	    (fun c x => by
216	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
217	      rw [map_mul]
218	      congr 1
219	      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
220	      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)
221	
222	@[simp]
223	lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
224	    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
225	  rfl

227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
241	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
242	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
246	
247	namespace DivisorAdaptation
248	
249	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
250	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
251	
252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
265	  toFinCoverData := D
266	  eqn := eqn
267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
289	            from rfl]
290	          exact E1
291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
299	          rw [E2]
300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
305	          rw [mul_assoc]
306	
307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
323	    exact h
324	  rw [hgerm]
325	  exact mul_mem
326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))

330	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
331	
332	/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
333	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
334	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
335	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
336	
337	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
339	through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
340	DEFINITION. -/
341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
343	  Ideal.span
344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
346	
347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
348	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
350	
351	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
352	the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
353	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
356	    (by
357	      intro a ha
358	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
366	
367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
371	    (by
372	      intro a ha
373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
381	
382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
385	
386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
388	
389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
391	  LinearMap.pi
392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
393	
394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
396	  LinearMap.pi
397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
398	
399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
405	
406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
414	
415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
417	
418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442	
443	end DivisorAdaptation
444	
445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
446	
447	variable (n : ℕ)
448	
449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
459	
460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
468	
469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)
473	
474	namespace DivFam
475	
476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
477	
478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
481	
482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
485	
486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
490	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
491	
492	@[simp]
493	lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
494	    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
495	  rfl
496	
497	end DivFam

9	/-!
10	# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation
11	
12	The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
13	of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
14	kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
15	relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
16	*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.
17	
18	This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
19	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
20	adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
21	**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
22	colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation
23	
24	* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
25	* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
26	* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
27	  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).
28	
29	What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
30	projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
31	(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
32	sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).
33	
34	This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
35	*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
36	time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
37	nonreduced base.
38	
39	## Main declarations
40	
41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
42	  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
44	  difference vanishes.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
46	  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.
47	-/
48

73	base-ring form of `DivisorFamilyFieldDegree`'s field-level lemma. -/
74	lemma toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' (i : A.index) :
75	    A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i :=
76	  rfl
77	
78	/-- **Support separation collapses the equalizer to the whole product, over any base
79	ring.** If the overlap colength modules vanish off the diagonal, every element of the
80	product of chart-local colengths satisfies the equalizer condition.
81	
82	The field-level statement (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated`) never used invertibility;
83	this is the same argument over `R`, which is what the DD-R gate consumes. -/
84	lemma gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'
85	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
86	    A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤ := by
87	  refine eq_top_iff.mpr fun s _ => ?_
88	  rw [mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]
89	  rintro ⟨i, j⟩
90	  by_cases hij : i = j
91	  · subst hij
92	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun f : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i i => (f : _ → _))
93	      (A.toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self' i)) (s i)

95	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
96	
97	/-- **The Čech difference vanishes for a support-separated adaptation.** Its kernel is the
98	whole product, and a linear map whose kernel is everything is zero. -/

100	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
101	    A.deltaLeft = A.deltaRight := by
102	  have h : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 := by

118	  haveI : Subsingleton (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) := by
119	    rw [A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep]
120	    infer_instance
121	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv
122	    (N := A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule) (M := PUnit.{u+1})
123	    (LinearEquiv.ofSubsingleton _ _)
124	
125	/-- (c4) for a support-separated adaptation: the Čech difference is the zero map, so its

127	product is.  In the seed setting that flatness is already landed
128	(`flat_ovlProd_of_seed`). -/
129	lemma flat_coker_diff_of_separated [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
130	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
131	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)) := by
132	  have hzero : A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight = 0 :=
133	    sub_eq_zero.mpr (A.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated hsep)
134	  rw [hzero, LinearMap.range_zero]
135	  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot ⊥ rfl)

137	/-! ## Separation is a statement about the support, not about the equations
138

140	the family support carries a unit equation, hence a unit overlap ideal, hence a vanishing

148	lemma subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (i j : A.index)

153	    rw [relResAlgHom_apply]
154	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
155	    intro z hz
156	    rw [(relCurve C R).presheaf.germ_res_apply]
157	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)

159	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)
160	  have htop : A.ovlIdeal i j = ⊤ :=
161	    Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)) hunit
162	  exact Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr htop

164	/-- **One support-meeting piece suffices.** If every piece other than `j₀` avoids the
165	support entirely, the adaptation is separated: any off-diagonal overlap involves a piece
166	missing the support, so the overlap misses it too. -/
167	lemma forall_subsingleton_ovlColength_of_unique_support_piece (j₀ : A.index)
168	    (hother : ∀ j : A.index, j ≠ j₀ →
169	      ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
170	    ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j) := by
171	  intro i j hij
172	  refine A.subsingleton_ovlColength_of_disjoint_supportLocus i j fun z hz => ?_
173	  by_cases hi : i = j₀
174	  · exact hother j (by rw [← hi]; exact fun h => hij h.symm) z hz.2
175	  · exact hother i hi z hz.1
176	
177	/-! ## The certificate -/
178	
179	/-- **The certificate of a support-separated adaptation.** With the off-diagonal overlap
180	colengths vanishing, the equalizer is the whole product, the Čech difference is zero, and
181	both flat-cokernel clauses hold automatically.  What is left is exactly the (c1) data —
182	each chart-local colength finite projective over `R` — plus the constant-rank reading,
183	which for the product is the sum of the per-piece ranks.
184	
185	This is the shape the pointwise gate can consume: no kernel-spanning hypothesis, and no
186	flatness of a Čech cokernel over a possibly nonreduced base. -/
187	theorem isCertified_of_separated {n : ℕ} [Module.Flat R A.ovlProd]
188	    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j))
189	    (hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j))
190	    (hproj : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j))
191	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
192	      ∑ᶠ j : A.index, Module.rankAtStalk (R := R) (A.colength j) p = n) :
193	    A.IsCertified n := by
194	  classical
195	  haveI := hfin
196	  haveI := hproj
197	  haveI : ∀ j : A.index, Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := fun _ =>
198	    Module.Flat.of_projective
199	  have htop := A.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated' hsep
200	  have hequiv : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.chartProd := A.gluedTopEquiv' htop
201	  haveI hprodProj : Module.Projective R A.chartProd :=
202	    Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.chartProd)
203	      (DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype R A.index (fun j => A.colength j))
204	  refine
205	    { finite_colength := hfin
206	      projective_colength := hproj
207	      finite_glued := Module.Finite.equiv hequiv.symm
208	      projective_glued := Module.Projective.of_equiv' (P := A.Glued) hequiv.symm
209	      rankAtStalk_glued := fun p => ?_
210	      flat_coker_incl := A.flat_coker_incl_of_separated hsep
211	      flat_coker_diff := A.flat_coker_diff_of_separated hsep }
212	  rw [Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv hequiv, Module.rankAtStalk_pi]
213	  exact hrank p

93	/-! ## The support locus of a local-equation system -/
94	
95	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
96	
97	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)
98	
99	/-- **The unit locus** of a local-equation system: the (open) union of the basic opens
100	of the equations — the locus where the divisor cut by `d` is trivial. -/
101	def unitLocus : X.Opens := ⨆ x, X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)
102	
103	lemma basicOpen_le_unitLocus (x : X) : X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) ≤ d.unitLocus :=
104	  le_iSup (fun x => X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)) x
105	
106	/-- Membership in the unit locus reads on ANY covering member containing the point:
107	`y ∈ unitLocus` iff the germ of `eqn x` at `y` is a unit, for every member `x` with
108	`y ∈ cover.opens x` (well-definedness across members is the ratio law). -/
109	lemma mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
110	    y ∈ d.unitLocus
111	      ↔ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) := by
112	  constructor
113	  · intro h
114	    obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp h
115	    have hy' : y ∈ d.cover.opens x' := X.basicOpen_le _ hx'
116	    have hu' : IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x') y hy').hom (d.eqn x')) :=
117	      (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy').mp hx'
118	    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := d.ratio_isUnit x x'
119	    have hyW : y ∈ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x' := ⟨hy, hy'⟩
120	    have h := congrArg
121	      ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x') y hyW).hom) hu
122	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
123	    rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
124	    exact ⟨u.isUnit.map _, hu'⟩
125	  · intro h
126	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x, (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr h⟩
127	
128	/-- **The support locus** of a local-equation system: the closed set of points where
129	the (well-defined) germ of the local equation fails to be a unit — the underlying set
130	of the divisor cut by `d`. -/
131	def supportLocus : Set X := (d.unitLocus : Set X)ᶜ
132	
133	lemma isClosed_supportLocus : IsClosed d.supportLocus :=
134	  d.unitLocus.isOpen.isClosed_compl
135	
136	lemma mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
137	    y ∈ d.supportLocus
138	      ↔ ¬ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) :=
139	  not_congr (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy)
140	
141	/-- **The per-member trace of the support**: on a covering member, the support locus is
142	the member minus the basic open of its equation. -/
143	lemma supportLocus_inter_opens (x : X) :
144	    d.supportLocus ∩ (d.cover.opens x : Set X)
145	      = (d.cover.opens x : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) : Set X) := by
146	  ext y
147	  constructor
148	  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hy⟩
149	    refine ⟨hy, fun hyb => hsupp (d.basicOpen_le_unitLocus x hyb)⟩
150	  · rintro ⟨hy, hyb⟩
151	    refine ⟨fun hyU => hyb ?_, hy⟩
152	    exact (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy).mp hyU)
153	
154	/-- **The support is closed over the base**: the image of the support locus under a
155	universally closed morphism (e.g. the structure morphism of the relative curve, from
156	the standing `IsProper C.hom`) is closed. -/
157	theorem isClosed_image_supportLocus (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] :
158	    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLocus) :=
159	  f.isClosedMap _ d.isClosed_supportLocus
160	
161	/-- **The support tube** (piece isolation, Zariski-locally on the base): for a
162	universally closed `f : X ⟶ S`, if the support fibre over a base point `s` is contained
163	in an open `U` (a union of adaptation pieces, in the DDR-4 instantiation), then there
164	is a Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `s` such that the whole support over `V` is contained
165	in `U`. -/
166	theorem exists_supportTube (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X}
167	    (hU : IsOpen U) {s : S} (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
168	    ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧ f.base ⁻¹' (V : Set S) ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
169	  obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hsV, hV⟩ := (f.isClosedMap).exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset
170	    d.isClosed_supportLocus hU hfib
171	  exact ⟨⟨V, hVopen⟩, hsV, hV⟩
172	
173	end Scheme.LocalEquations
174	
175	/-! ## The licence: properness of the relative curve over an arbitrary test ring -/
176	
177	section RelCurveProper
178	
179	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
180	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
181	
182	/-- **Base change of properness to an arbitrary test ring**: the second projection of
183	`C ⊗ Spec R` is proper, for every commutative `k`-algebra `R` — the general-`R` form of
184	`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.instIsProperSndLeft` (which is keyed on field extensions).
185	This is the DDR-4 support-tube licence over the `Z(♦)`-chart rings `R_Z`. -/
186	instance instIsProperRelSndLeft : IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left :=
187	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsProper)
188	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
189	
190	/-- The properness instance, keyed on the `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` spelling installed by
191	`relCurve.instOver` (definitionally the second projection). In particular
192	`UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution, which is what
193	`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` consumes. -/
194	instance instIsProperRelCurveHom :
195	    IsProper ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) :=
196	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left)
197	
198	/-- Acceptance smoke test: the support tube applies to the relative curve over an
199	arbitrary test ring with the universally-closed instance found by resolution. -/
200	private theorem supportTube_smoke (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
201	    {U : Set (relCurve C R)} (hU : IsOpen U) {s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)}
202	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus
203	      ⊆ U) :
204	    ∃ V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).Opens, s ∈ V ∧
205	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' (V : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
206	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U :=
207	  d.exists_supportTube _ hU hfib
208	
209	end RelCurveProper

225	companion of `ThetaGeneratorSeed.flat_sections_piece`. -/
226	theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
227	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) := by
228	  cases j with
229	  | inl j =>
230	      exact flat_sections_basicOpen R (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
231	        (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π false) (D.h₀ j)

246	    IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) w hwj).hom (A.eqn j))
247	      ↔ IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens w) w
248	          (d.cover.mem_opens w)).hom (d.eqn w)) := by
249	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j w

19	flattening criterion shows that the condition implies target-cokernel flatness.
20	Consequently, merely choosing the actual kernel does not evade the nonreduced-base
21	gate: its fibre-spanning law is equivalent to the flatness one is trying to prove.
22	No fibrewise image-persistence statement is used as a substitute for this law.
23	-/
24	
25	set_option autoImplicit false
26	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8
28	set_option maxRecDepth 8000
29	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false

32	
33	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
34	open scoped TensorProduct

36	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

38	open Scheme Grassmannian

40	/-! ## The `rTensor` form of flat-cokernel purity -/
41	
42	section KernelSpan
43	
44	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
45	variable {M N : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N]
46	  [Module R M] [Module R N]
47	
48	/-- Kernel spanning after base change is equivalent to injectivity after first
49	dividing the source by the global kernel.  This is pure linear algebra and holds
50	for an arbitrary coefficient module `A`.
51	
52	The forward direction lifts through the right-exact base change of the quotient
53	map.  The reverse direction observes that an element in the fibre kernel has zero
54	image in the fibre of the injectivization, hence already lies in the fibre image
55	of the global kernel. -/
56	theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective
57	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
58	    LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor A) ≤
59	        LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker f).subtype.rTensor A) ↔
60	      Function.Injective
61	        (((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A) := by
62	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
63	  have hcomp : f.rTensor A =
64	      (L.liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A ∘ₗ L.mkQ.rTensor A := by
65	    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
66	  have hexact : Function.Exact (L.subtype.rTensor A) (L.mkQ.rTensor A) :=
67	    rTensor_exact A (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ L) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L)
68	  constructor
69	  · intro hspan
70	    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
71	    intro w hw
72	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.rTensor_surjective A
73	      (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
74	    have hfx : f.rTensor A x = 0 := by
75	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
76	      exact hw
77	    have hx := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
78	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker] at hx
79	    exact hx
80	  · intro hinj x hx
81	    have hzero : L.mkQ.rTensor A x = 0 := by
82	      apply hinj
83	      rw [map_zero]
84	      have hfx := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx
85	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply] at hfx
86	      exact hfx
87	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker]
88	    exact hzero

90	variable {P : Type u} [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P]
91	
92	/-- An independent boundary presentation of every base-changed kernel makes
93	the injectivized map remain injective after that base change.  This is the
94	non-circular bridge from a fibrewise Koszul theorem to the relative flatness
95	criterion: no flatness of the cokernel is assumed.
96	
97	The proof lifts through the right-exact base change of `ker(f).mkQ`.  A lift
98	in the fibre kernel is a base-changed boundary by `hspan`, and the global
99	identity `f ∘ d = 0` makes its quotient class vanish. -/
100	theorem liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_boundary
101	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
102	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
103	    (hspan : LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.baseChange S f) ≤
104	      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S d)) :
105	    Function.Injective
106	      (LinearMap.baseChange S ((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl)) := by
107	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
108	  let fbar := L.liftQ f le_rfl
109	  have hfcomp : LinearMap.baseChange S f =
110	      (LinearMap.baseChange S fbar).comp (LinearMap.baseChange S L.mkQ) := by
111	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
112	  have hdL : ∀ y : P, d y ∈ L := by
113	    intro y
114	    apply LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr
115	    have hy := LinearMap.congr_fun hfd y
116	    simpa only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply] using hy
117	  have hqd : L.mkQ.comp d = 0 := by
118	    apply LinearMap.ext
119	    intro y
120	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply,
121	      Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
122	    exact hdL y
123	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
124	  intro w hw
125	  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.baseChange_surjective S
126	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
127	  have hfx : LinearMap.baseChange S f x = 0 := by
128	    rw [hfcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
129	    exact hw
130	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
131	  rw [← hy, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hqd,
132	    LinearMap.baseChange_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]
133	
134	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
135	-- Elaborating the quotient injectivization through tensor purity exceeds the default budget.
136	/-- Flatness of the target cokernel forces the fibre kernel to be generated by
137	the base-changed global kernel.  Indeed, the injectivization
138	`M ⧸ ker δ → N` has cokernel `N ⧸ range δ`; flatness of that cokernel makes the
139	injectivization universally injective. -/
140	theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_of_flat_range_quotient
141	    (δ : M →ₗ[R] N)
142	    [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
143	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
144	    LinearMap.ker (δ.rTensor A) ≤
145	      LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.rTensor A) := by
146	  apply (ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective δ A).mpr
147	  set fbar := (LinearMap.ker δ).liftQ δ le_rfl with hfbar
148	  have hfbar_inj : Function.Injective fbar := by
149	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, hfbar]
150	    exact Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot' _ δ rfl
151	  have hexact : Function.Exact fbar (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ := by
152	    rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.ker_mkQ, hfbar, Submodule.range_liftQ]
153	  have hleft : Function.Injective (fbar.lTensor A) :=
154	    LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
155	      (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
156	      fbar hfbar_inj hexact A
157	  exact (LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj (M := A) (f := fbar)).mp hleft
158	
159	end KernelSpan

181	  ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) ⊤))

200	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n)) :

211	/-- The canonical kernel syzygy is finite at every high window.  This uses only
212	Noetherianity of the carve-chart ring and finiteness of the preceding relation
213	module; it does not assert that its formation commutes with residue fields. -/
214	theorem finite_divUniversalHighWindowKernelSyzygy (n : Nat)
215	    (K : Submodule RZ
216	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
217	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))
218	    [Module.Finite RZ K] :
219	    Module.Finite RZ

221	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) := by
222	  letI := finite_divUniversalHighWindowMulSource
223	    (C := C) (pi := pi) hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K
224	  infer_instance

227	-- The fibrewise equivalence elaborates a dependent quotient map at every prime.
228	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
229	-- Residue-field tensor instances over the carve ring need the larger local budget.
230	/-- For the canonical kernel candidate, `DivUniversalHighWindowSyzygySpans` is
231	equivalent to residue-fibre injectivity of the injectivized multiplication map.
232	This is the precise rank/minor condition a relative persistence argument must
233	establish; fieldwise image persistence alone does not imply it. -/
234	theorem divUniversalHighWindowKernelSyzygySpans_iff (n : Nat)
235	    (K : Submodule RZ
236	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
237	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n)) :
238	    DivUniversalHighWindowSyzygySpans (C := C) (pi := pi)
239	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K
240	        (divUniversalHighWindowKernelSyzygy (C := C) (pi := pi)
241	          hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) ↔
242	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum RZ,
243	        Function.Injective
244	          (((divUniversalHighWindowKernelSyzygy (C := C) (pi := pi)
245	              hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K).liftQ

252	      (divUniversalHighWindowMulMap (C := C) (pi := pi)
253	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) p.asIdeal.ResidueField).mp (h.2 p)

255	    refine ⟨le_rfl, fun p => ?_⟩
256	    exact (ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective
257	      (divUniversalHighWindowMulMap (C := C) (pi := pi)
258	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) p.asIdeal.ResidueField).mpr (h p)

261	-- Specializing tensor purity to the dependent high-window map is elaboration-heavy.
262	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
263	-- The target quotient's flatness instance unfolds the complete high-window ambient.
264	/-- The actual kernel of a high-window multiplication presentation is a valid
265	relative syzygy module if its target quotient is flat.  This is the purity
266	direction and does not infer flatness from fibrewise persistence. -/

268	    (n : Nat)
269	    (K : Submodule RZ
270	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)
271	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))

273	      (divUniversalHighWindowAmbient (C := C) (pi := pi) (hpi := hpi) (g := g)

279	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) := by

284	      (divUniversalHighWindowMulMap (C := C) (pi := pi)
285	        hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 i j n K) p.asIdeal.ResidueField

/-

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyField
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OpenImmersionUnits

/-!
# The colength↔degree identity for divisor families over a field (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f))

Over a field `K` the forward map `divFamDivisor` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyField`)
sends a certified divisor family to its Weil divisor. This file lands the **degree identity**

`deg K (divFamDivisor F) = finrank K W(d)`

(so, with the field half `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.finrank_glued`, `deg = n`), the
colength↔degree bridge across the glued equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺)`.

## The support-separated assembly

The equalizer does not decompose over the cover naively — a supported closed point may lie in
two pieces. This file proves the **support-separated** case, which is the one the DD-1c backward
map consumes (its adaptations isolate the support points by construction): when the overlap
colength modules vanish (`ovlColength i j` is subsingleton for `i ≠ j`), the equalizer is the
*whole* product of the chart-local colengths, so

`finrank K W(d) = ∑ⱼ finrank K (Γ(D(hⱼ)) ⧸ (fⱼ))`  (`finrank_glued_eq_sum_of_separated`),

pure module algebra (`Module.finrank_pi_fintype` over the field, where every factor is free).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
open Module (finrank)

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## A unit-germ ↔ trivial-order dictionary on the curve bundle

Reusable core: on the curve bundle `X/K`, a section `f` over an open `U ∋ η` is a unit at a
closed point `z ∈ U` exactly when the order at `z` of its germ at `η` is trivial. Both
directions of the private `ChartColength` machinery, packaged as a public equivalence through
the DVR valuation of the stalk. -/

namespace Scheme

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]

/-- **Unit germ ↔ trivial order.** For a section `f` over an open `U ∋ η` whose germ at `η` is
the field unit `g`, the germ of `f` at a closed point `z ∈ U` is a unit of the stalk exactly
when the order of `g` at `z` is trivial (`ordZ = 1`). -/
theorem isUnit_germ_iff_ordZ_eq_one {U : X.Opens} (hη : genericPoint X ∈ U)
    (f : Γ(X, U)) (g : X.functionFieldˣ)
    (hg : (g : X.functionField) = (X.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hη).hom f)
    {z : X} (hz : z ∈ U) (hzg : z ≠ genericPoint X) :
    IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ U z hz).hom f)
      ↔ Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg g = 1 := by
  rw [Scheme.ordZ_eq_one_iff]
  letI := isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg
  letI := isDedekindDomain_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg
  have hord : Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg
      = (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField := rfl
  have hgs : (X.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hη).hom f
      = algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField
          ((X.presheaf.germ U z hz).hom f) := by
    rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    exact (X.presheaf.germ_stalkSpecializes_apply hz
      ((genericPoint_spec X).specializes trivial) f).symm
  rw [hg, hgs, hord, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_eq_one_iff_notMem]
  exact (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal).symm

/-- A unit in a closed-point stalk remains a unit in the function field, hence has
trivial `ordZ`.  This is the valuation form of the stalk-unit transition bridge used
when comparing a pulled local equation with a theta-chart reading. -/
theorem ordZ_unitsMap_stalk_eq_one {z : X} (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X)
    (v : (X.presheaf.stalk z)ˣ) :
    Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
      (Units.map (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField).toMonoidHom v) = 1 := by
  rw [Scheme.ordZ_eq_one_iff (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz]
  exact Valuation.Integers.one_of_isUnit'
    (v := Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz)
    v.isUnit (fun y => Scheme.ord_algebraMap_stalk_le_one K hz y)

/-- Multiplication by the function-field image of a stalk unit does not change the
additive order at the closed point. -/
theorem toAdd_ordZ_mul_unitsMap_stalk {z : X} (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X)
    (a : X.functionFieldˣ) (v : (X.presheaf.stalk z)ˣ) :
    Multiplicative.toAdd
        (Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
          (a * Units.map (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField).toMonoidHom v))
      = Multiplicative.toAdd (Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz a) := by
  rw [map_mul, ordZ_unitsMap_stalk_eq_one K hz v, mul_one]

end Scheme

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {d : (relCurve C K).LocalEquations} (A : DivisorAdaptation C K π d)

/-- On the diagonal `i = i` the two overlap-restriction maps of the equalizer coincide: the two
`≤`-witnesses `pieces i ⊓ pieces i ≤ pieces i` are definitionally equal (proof irrelevance), so
`toOvlLeft i i` and `toOvlRight i i` are the same map. -/
lemma toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self (i : A.index) :
    A.toOvlLeft i i = A.toOvlRight i i :=
  rfl

/-- **Support separation collapses the equalizer to the whole product.** If the overlap colength
modules vanish off the diagonal (`ovlColength i j` subsingleton for `i ≠ j`), then every element
of the product of chart-local colengths satisfies the equalizer condition, so the glued
submodule is all of `∏ⱼ colength j`. -/
lemma gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated
    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :
    A.gluedSubmodule = ⊤ := by
  refine eq_top_iff.mpr fun s _ => ?_
  rw [mem_gluedSubmodule_iff]

records the resulting statement.

conclusion is monotone in the neighbourhood, so shrinking `V` to a basic open inside it
preserves support isolation.

`DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean` reduced the DD-R certificate gate to *away-local* certificates
over a span-`⊤` family.  The geometry that produces such certificates, however, is
pointwise on the base: the support tube (`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube`)
isolates the pieces over a Zariski neighbourhood **of one base point at a time**, and the
fibre analyses all read at a single `p : PrimeSpectrum R`.

This file closes that gap with the quasi-compactness step.  If for every prime `p` there
is some `r ∉ p` over whose away localization the system is certified, then the good
elements span the unit ideal (their basic opens cover `Spec R`), so finitely many of them
already do — and `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` applies.

The result is that the certificate gate for the DD-R endgame is now genuinely *pointwise*:
one base point at a time, exactly the shape the landed fibre machinery delivers.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate
  for a bare local-equation system.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_away_certified`
  — the seed form.

/-- **Pointwise good elements span the unit ideal, finitely.** If a predicate `P` on `R`
holds at some element outside each prime, then finitely many elements satisfying `P` span

needs: the basic opens of the good elements cover the spectrum, hence the good set spans
the unit ideal, hence `1` is a finite combination of good elements. -/
theorem exists_fin_span_eq_top_of_forall_prime (P : R → Prop)
    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, ∃ r, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ P r) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ i, P (g i) := by

  -- the good elements span the unit ideal, because their basic opens cover `Spec R`

  -- `1` is then a finite combination of good elements

    show (1 : R) ∈ Ideal.span {r : R | P r}

whose membership predicate is `IsLocallyCertified`: some span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R`
carries certified families over the localizations `Localization.Away (g i)` which are
divisor-equal to the pulled system.  **Nothing downstream of `DivFamZar` asks for a
certificate over `R` itself.**

The certificate-assembly lane has nevertheless been attacking the *global* clause

is exactly the hypothesis that is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (I-0209: a piece
whose support trace leaks has a non-finite colength, and the localization repair breaks
finiteness over `R`).  The lane has been paying for a strictly stronger statement than
its consumer needs.

This file lands the relaxation.  `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` says: to
certify a system *Zariski-locally* it suffices to produce, for each member of some
span-`⊤` family, a certified family over that localization which is divisor-equal to the
pulled system.  Then `ThetaGeneratorSeed.isLocallyCertified_of_forall_away_isCertified`

localizing at each member of a span-`⊤` family** — which is precisely what the support

certified, and hence has a `DivFamZar` class.

produced from local data and that the seed's pulled system over an away localization is

* `AlgebraicGeometry.ThetaGeneratorSeed.divFamZar_of_forall_away_certified` — the

-/

/-!
# The general colength↔degree identity over a field (the Mayer–Vietoris wall, I-0179)

For an ARBITRARY divisor adaptation `A` of a local-equation system `d` on the relative curve
over a field `K` — no support-separation hypothesis — this file proves

`deg K (div d) = finrank K W(d)`   (`DivisorAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor`),

the general colength↔degree identity threaded as `hdeg` through the G-1 keystones
(`Picard/DivisorThetaFibreData.lean`) and the field dictionary
(`divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj`, `Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean`).

## The CRT route (why the wall falls)

The glued equalizer `W(d) ⊆ Π_j Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)` does not decompose over the cover naively —
a supported point may be seen by several pieces.  The resolution
(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyStalkEval`): decompose into **stalk** quotients
`𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)`, which are chart-independent — on the equalizer, every piece seeing `z`
reads the same stalk value (`stalkColEval_glued`).  Then:

* per piece, `Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j) ≅ Π_{z ∈ supp ∩ D(h_j)} 𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)`
  (`pieceStalkEval_bijective`): injectivity is the stalk-locality of regular principal
  ideals (`Scheme.mem_span_singleton_of_forall_germ`), surjectivity is a dimension count —
  the landed per-piece degree reading (`finrank_colength_eq_sum`) against the pointwise
  stalk dictionary (`finrank_stalkQuot_eq_coeffAt_mul`), an honest CRT with no new
  constructions;
* globally, `W(d) ≅ Π_{z ∈ supp} 𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)` (`gluedStalkEval_injective` +
  `gluedStalkEval_surjective`): the equalizer condition makes the per-piece local values
  agree at shared points, and conversely any family of stalk values assembles to an
  equalizer element piece by piece.

Summing `finrank K (𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)) = coeff_z(D) · [κ(z) : K]` over the support gives the
degree.  Since the left-hand side `deg K (div d)` is adaptation-free and the identity holds
for EVERY adaptation of `d`, adaptation-independence of the glued rank is a corollary, not
an input — the circularity of the refine-to-separated shortcut (I-0179) is dissolved.

## Consequences

* `deg_divFamDivisor` — `deg K (divFamDivisor F) = n` for every certified family
  `F : DivFam C K π n` (the `hdeg` input of `divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj`, unconditional).
* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor` — the field-level seam shape.
* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor_pulledEquations` — the exact
  fibrewise form consumed by G-1: for a certified adaptation over any test ring, the divisor
  cut on the `K`-fibre by the pulled equations has degree `n` (certificates base-change,
  `isCertified_pullback`).
-/

/-!
# The support-tube finiteness engine: the (c1)-finite production brick (G-4)

The algebraic half of the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) (`informal/w4-g4-worksheet.md`
§3, the one row with no landed engine): for a divisor adaptation over a test ring `R`,
the chart-local colength `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is a **finite** `R`-module — Kleiman's
finiteness-of-the-divisor-subscheme step, per piece.

## The honest hypothesis (probe finding)

The colength is the section ring of the piece trace of the family support
(`supportLocus_inter_pieces`): the closed subscheme of the affine piece `D(h_j)` cut by
`f_j`, whose underlying set is `D(h_j) \ D(f_j) = supportLocus ∩ D(h_j)`.  The engine
input is that this trace is **closed in the whole relative curve**; universal closedness
of the curve over the base (the landed licence `instIsProperRelCurveHom`) then makes the
trace universally closed over `Spec R`, and a universally closed affine morphism of
finite type is finite (`IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom` +
`IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType` — the mathlib heart, the
`SlicingFlatKernel` luck again).  No Noetherian hypothesis anywhere.

Fibrewise finiteness data alone (each fibre colength artinian, even of constant total
dimension) canNOT replace the closed-trace input.  Guard examples:

* `Γ(𝔸¹) = k[x]` over `k` with `f = 0`: excluded by `[UniversallyClosed]` on the
  structure morphism (the affine line is not proper).
* the hyperbola `k[t,x]⧸(tx−1)` over `k[t]` inside `X = ℙ¹_{k[t]}`, piece the affine
  chart: every fibre colength is artinian, the module is even flat, yet not finite —
  the closure of the trace leaks into `(∞, t=0)`, so the closed-trace hypothesis fails
  exactly where it must.
* two disjoint base sections with a piece missing one point of one section: piece
  colength `k[t] × k[t,t⁻¹]`, all fibre colengths artinian of constant total dimension
  `2` on the glued module — the PER-PIECE trace leaks.  Hence the certificate's
  per-piece clause genuinely constrains the adaptation, and the fibrewise input of
  P-fib-N enters this brick only through its topological shadow, the **no-leak fibre
  criterion** threaded below (`hfib` of
  `finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset`).

## Main declarations

* `Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLeak` — the leak locus of a support trace out of an
  open `U`: `closure (supportLocus ∩ U) \ U`, closed
  (`isClosed_supportLeak`), with `isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`
  and the fibre criterion `supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre`;
* `Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_image_supportLeak` — the tube-side product: the base
  image of the leak locus is closed under a universally closed structure morphism, so
  its complement is the Zariski-open base locus where the trace is closed;
* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed` — **the
  abstract engine**: `V` affine open in `X` over `Spec R`, structure morphism
  universally closed and locally of finite type, `V \ D(g)` closed in `X` ⟹
  `Γ(X, V) ⧸ (g)` is a finite `R`-module (via the closed immersion
  `Spec (Γ(X, V) ⧸ (g)) ⟶ X` and mathlib's integral = universally closed + affine);
* `DivisorAdaptation.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter` /
  `finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty` /
  `finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset` /
  `finite_colength_of_supportLocus_subset` — **the (c1)-finite clause** for the piece

The `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through the
`Over` structure (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate the same
instances.
-/

    IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion _ (hrange ▸ hclosed)
  have hfin : IsFinite ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {g}))) ≫ hV.fromSpec)
        ≫ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))) := by
    rw [IsFinite.iff_isIntegralHom_and_locallyOfFiniteType,
      IsIntegralHom.iff_universallyClosed_and_isAffineHom]
    exact ⟨⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩
  rw [Category.assoc, hV.specMap_quotient_mk_fromSpec_over] at hfin
  exact RingHom.finite_algebraMap.mp ((IsFinite.SpecMap_iff _).mp hfin)

end IsAffineOpen

/-! ## The adaptation corollaries: the (c1)-finite clause per piece -/

section Adaptation

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k}

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable [IsFinite π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

/-- **The (c1)-finite clause from a closed support trace** (the core adaptation
corollary): if the piece trace of the family support is closed in the relative curve,
the chart-local colength `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is a finite `R`-module — the
`IsCertified.finite_colength` clause at `j`, and the `[Module.Finite]` input of the
landed `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField`.  Consumes the properness
licence (`instIsProperRelCurveHom`); no Noetherian hypothesis. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter (j : A.index)
    (hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := by
  rw [A.supportLocus_inter_pieces j] at hclosed
  exact (A.toFinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces j).finite_quotient_span_singleton_of_isClosed
    (A.eqn j) hclosed

/-- The (c1)-finite clause in the leak-locus spelling: nothing leaks out of the piece
`j`, so the trace is closed and the colength is finite. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty (j : A.index)
    (hleak : d.supportLeak (A.pieces j) = ∅) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter j
    ((d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mpr hleak)

/-- **The (c1)-finite clause from fibrewise no-leak data** (the CertUniv threading
slot): if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the piece trace stays in
the piece — the topological shadow of the P-fib-N fibrewise finiteness data combined
with the seed design — then the colength of the piece `j` is a finite `R`-module. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset (j : A.index)
    (hfib : ∀ s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R),
      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))
        ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
    (d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre
      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) hfib)

/-- The (c1)-finite clause when the piece dominates the support: if the whole family
support lies in the piece `j` (the shape the support tube produces after shrinking the
base), the colength is finite.  The fibrewise form `∀ s, fibre ∩ supportLocus ⊆ piece`
reduces to this hypothesis by `fun x hx => hfib _ ⟨rfl, hx⟩`. -/
theorem finite_colength_of_supportLocus_subset (j : A.index)
    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.finite_colength_of_isClosed_supportLocus_inter j (by
    rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus)

end DivisorAdaptation

end Adaptation

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- A ring equivalence carries nonzerodivisors to nonzerodivisors. -/
private lemma map_mem_nonZeroDivisors {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (e : A ≃+* B) {x : A} (hx : x ∈ nonZeroDivisors A) :
    e x ∈ nonZeroDivisors B := by
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff] at hx ⊢
  obtain ⟨hl, hr⟩ := hx
  constructor
  · intro y hy
    have h := congrArg e.symm hy
    rw [map_mul, map_zero, e.symm_apply_apply] at h
    have hy0 : e.symm y = 0 := hl _ h
    calc y = e (e.symm y) := (e.apply_symm_apply y).symm
      _ = 0 := by rw [hy0, map_zero]
  · intro y hy
    have h := congrArg e.symm hy
    rw [map_mul, map_zero, e.symm_apply_apply] at h
    have hy0 : e.symm y = 0 := hr _ h
    calc y = e (e.symm y) := (e.apply_symm_apply y).symm
      _ = 0 := by rw [hy0, map_zero]

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

    (b : Bool) (g : Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R pi b)) :
    L ⊗[R] Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen g) ≃ₐ[L]
      Γ(relCurve C L,
        (relCurve C L).basicOpen (relPinnedSectionsMap C R L pi b g)) :=
  match b with
  | false =>
      pieceTermBaseChangeAlg L (fiberChart₀ pi)
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isCompact
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isQuasiSeparated
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover pi))
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C L (fiberTwoCover pi)) g
  | true =>

    (L : Type u) [CommRing L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower k R L]

/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
  side : relCurve C R → Bool
  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)

lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z

lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)

/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)

/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)

/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
restricted to the piece. -/
noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)

/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):

* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).

Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
structure IsGenerator : Prop where
  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
      nonZeroDivisors
